description: A Legal Director for Strategic Partnerships must approve the final agreement for a three-year joint research collaboration between the company and a university partner, including control of background technology and publication of research results. The agreement affects the company's future commercial rights and its ability to protect sensitive patient-related information.

shared_context.S1: The company and a university partner are negotiating a three-year joint research agreement to develop diagnostic software.
shared_context.S2: The current draft grants the university partner an exclusive commercial license to all background technology used in the project and permits publication of project results.
shared_context.S3: The parties expect to sign after final legal approval next month.
shared_context.S4: Company policy requires the Intellectual Property Counsel and Privacy and Clinical Regulatory Counsel to give a readout before the Legal Director approves a strategic research agreement.

PF1.text: Elias reviewed the university's master research agreement and confirmed that background patents U1, U2, and U3 are licensed to the company only for noncommercial academic use; the final agreement must exclude those three patents from any commercial license and require separate written university consent before commercial use. The university supplied the controlling schedule overnight, so Elias has not yet incorporated it into the draft or circulated the finding.

PF2.text: Nadia confirmed with the product lead and privacy office in yesterday's working session that the company's non-negotiable clinical-data position is to prohibit publication containing patient-level data and to require de-identification before any permitted external publication. The working-session minutes have not yet been circulated to the deal team.

acceptance_conditions: The agreement must not receive unconditional approval while the required protective revisions remain pending.
Patents U1, U2, and U3 must be excluded from the commercial background-IP license, and separate written consent must be required before their commercial use.
Separate written university consent must be required before commercial use of U1, U2, or U3.
Publication containing patient-level data must be prohibited.
Any permitted external publication must require de-identification first.
At least one agreement revision or related implementation commitment must be documented.

content_checks.C2: 'U1' in decisions['background_ip_treatment'] and 'U2' in decisions['background_ip_treatment'] and 'U3' in decisions['background_ip_treatment'] and (decisions['commercial_use_consent_required'] == True or 'written consent' in decisions['background_ip_treatment'])

decisive_facts.why: The university schedule changes the background-IP choice from licensing all background technology to excluding exactly U1, U2, and U3 and requiring separate written consent before their commercial use.

The product and privacy confirmation changes the publication terms from the draft's unrestricted permission to a prohibition on patient-level data and a requirement for de-identification before any permitted external publication.
